# phase-086 — Make `xs.map(f)` work when the receiver is a variable

## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
src/interpreter.rs:2052 matches `Expr::Variable(name) => name.clone()` FIRST inside `call_method`, so a variable receiver never reaches the list branch at src/interpreter.rs:2059-2071 whose own comment reads '`xs.map(f)` is the method spelling of the higher-order builtin' - the case that comment names is precisely the case it cannot see. The dotted name is resolved as a module-style builtin, `xs.map` becomes `xs_map`, and nothing registers it. Verified against the built binary this audit: after `to dbl(x) give back x * 2 end` and `set xs to [1,2,3]`, `say xs.map(dbl)` raises `RuntimeError: Unknown function 'xs_map'` at 5:1 - on the tree-walker AND through `rb compile` + `rb vm`, while the literal receiver `[1,2,3].map(dbl)` prints `[2, 4, 6]`. src/bytecode/vm.rs:2707 `call_method` has the same shape and fails identically, so a one-engine fix would be caught by tests/differential_test.rs. SPEC.md:574-579 presents `set doubled to numbers.map(double)` as the entire headline example of '### First-Class Functions': the one program the specification uses to introduce function values is the one program that does not run.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Make `xs.map(f)` answer on both engines for a variable receiver, so the specification's own first-class-functions example runs.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-086
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `rb run` on SPEC.md:574-579 verbatim prints the doubled list, and `rb compile` + `rb vm` on the same file prints the same list
- [ ] the two engines agree across three tests - `xs.map(f)`, `list.map(xs, f)` and `[1,2,3].map(f)` - each asserting the same literal expected value
- [ ] bad arguments stay clean RuntimeErrors, not panics: `xs.map(5)` names the argument it got and `xs.map()` with no argument is a RuntimeError
- [ ] a module receiver is unaffected: `text.uppercase("hi")` and `files.exists(p)` still answer, in tests that fail if the fix shadows them
- [ ] an object receiver is unaffected: a method on an object declared with `object`/`has`/`to` still dispatches, and the existing object-model tests stay green
- [ ] edge_* tests cover: an empty list receiver, a singleton receiver, a list held in a record field, a list returned from a function, a receiver whose name collides with a module name in src/stdlib.rs:19, and a receiver whose value is `nothing`
- [ ] `cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean
